_meta.purpose: Validation set for ASTRANOVUS. Positives are Earth sites NASA publishes as planetary-analog field sites. Controls are lowland, vegetated or humid regions chosen BY CONSTRUCTION to be poor analogs (no citation: this is a sanity check, not evidence). The target mapping (which Moon/Mars reference each site should resemble) is an ASTRANOVUS judgement and is flagged as such.
_meta.coordinates: Approximate site centres in decimal degrees. The Earth grid has 2.5 degree cells, so each site is evaluated at its nearest grid cell, which is far coarser than the site itself.

cohorts.v1: sites scored and examined before this protocol existed (their results were visible during development, so they are not pristine held-out data)
cohorts.v2_prospective: sites added after the v1 diagnostics; first scored by this run and reported separately; never used for any rule change

citation.text: NASA Science: researchers collect soil samples in Chile's Atacama Desert to study conditions relevant to Mars; NASA lists Atacama among analog field sites.
NASA-led Haughton-Mars Project: barren, freezing, isolated polar-desert terrain used to simulate Mars (and Moon) exploration.
NASA Science: researchers map lava tubes at Lava Beds National Monument with GPR, magnetometers and seismometers, linked to Moon and Mars.
NASA analog missions page: Hawaii's Kilauea Volcano is a planetary analog site used to simulate Moon and Mars conditions.
NASA: Iceland has served as a lunar stand-in for astronaut geology training since Apollo (1967), and the Artemis II crew trained there in 2024; both Iceland and the Moon feature basalts and breccias.
NASA Science highlights drone and field tests in Death Valley as planetary-analog testing.
NASA/JPL field-tested the ERNEST prototype rover in the Colorado Desert (March 2026) for future Moon (and possibly Mars) rovers.

NASA NTRS: the McMurdo Dry Valleys are the best-known Earth analog of the Martian high-northern plains where Phoenix landed (ground ice, permafrost, instrument testing); NASA Astrobiology describes Beacon and University Valley ice-cemented ground as Mars analogs.
NASA Goddard: the Arctic Mars Analogue Svalbard Expedition (AMASE) has tested flight-like Mars instruments and studied basaltic carbonates (ALH84001-like) at Svalbard sites since 2003.

positives.name: Craters of the Moon National Monument, Idaho, USA

citation.text: US National Park Service: Apollo 14 crew members visited in August 1969 to study volcanic geology (the NPS FAQ notes they did not formally train there); NASA Earth Observatory describes the lava landscape as lunar-like. Basaltic lava field with lava tubes.

positives.limitation: Basalt field analog for geology/lava-tube morphology only; semi-arid with sagebrush cover, not a thermal or ice analog.

positives.name: Mars Desert Research Station area (San Rafael Swell), Utah, USA

citation.text: NASA NTRS / NASA Astrobiology Institute reports describe the Morrison Formation area around MDRS as an analogue for Mars geomorphology and sedimentary processes (soil cores from the main geologic units).

positives.limitation: Sedimentary-geology and crew-operations analog; semi-arid and mild, so a weak match for Jezero's cold, thermal and igneous character.

controls.name: Siberian taiga (cold but forested)
controls.why: cold like the polar analogs but vegetated and wet: should rank below tundra/polar desert for ice targets

controls.name: US Great Plains grassland
controls.why: semi-arid but vegetated farmland: should rank below true deserts for dry-barren targets

controls.name: Sahel savanna
controls.why: hot and seasonally dry but vegetated: neighbours the Sahara without being a barren analog

controls.name: Mediterranean scrub (Spain)
controls.why: dry summers but vegetated and mild

controls.name: Greenland ice sheet
controls.why: cold and dry but ice-covered: fails the bare-ground criterion of dry geology/rover targets

controls.name: East Antarctic plateau
controls.why: cold and dry but ice-covered: no exposed ground

controls.name: Central Sahara
controls.why: matches aridity and bare ground but not temperature or ice: a regions-that-match-dryness-but-not-cold control

controls.name: Guiana Highlands (rugged but humid, forested)
controls.why: rugged terrain but wet and forested: matches terrain, fails aridity and barrenness

hypotheses_pakistan._note: From the original TerraTwin proposal. HYPOTHESES only: coordinates approximate, no NASA analog citation retrieved, 2.5-degree cells far too coarse to resolve these sites. Reported but never counted as validation.

sites.name: Hingol mud volcanoes
sites.literature_note: A satellite-imagery study indexed by ITU reports >80 mud volcanoes in Pakistan clustered in Hingol National Park. No source retrieved uses Hingol as a Mars analog; the closest Mars-analog comparisons in retrieved sources are Azerbaijan and the Gulf of Cadiz (Allen and Oehler, NASA JSC).
